title: Trump’s Culture War, Amid Setbacks, Will Soon Face a Hostile Congress
summary: The White House campaign to make major changes at the Smithsonian and the Kennedy Center has fallen short of its goals. Will it be further disrupted by a Democrat-led Congress?

President Trump has waged a fierce culture war in Washington during the first half of his second term, assailing some institutions and programs for their “wokeness” and trying to align them with his own agenda.


He tried to fire the director of the National Portrait Gallery and stamp out “improper ideology” at the Smithsonian Institution.


At the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, he and his allies are fighting to put his name on the building, which was created as a memorial for a slain president.


He is also[continuing to push for a two-year closure](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/31/arts/kennedy-center-trump-beatty.html) of the center’s main building for a $250 million renovation.


Image


President Trump’s name was added to the Kennedy Center, then removed by judicial order. The tarp erected in the summer as part of the removal is still up at the building.


Credit...


Annabelle Gordon/Reuters


Those efforts, and others, have produced a few victories for the administration but have also been met with public protests, boycotts, legal battles and[judicial injunctions.](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/29/arts/kennedy-center-trump-name-remove.html) Now, after a major loss for Republicans in the midterm elections, Mr. Trump must also reckon with redrawn lines of power in Congress, where Democrats will soon have much more control over cultural funding, oversight panels and appointments to the Smithsonian’s governing Board of Regents.
